audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as entirely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $794.2 million bridge addition, equal to $14.35 per share and 12.5% of base equity value; $71.6 million was held in Belarus and Ukraine
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments to common-equity value without deducting minimum operating liquidity, trapped balances or distribution taxes.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary uses of cash from operating activities include compensation to our employees and related costs, payments for leased facilities, various general corporate expenditures and income tax payments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved excess-cash question, not a demonstrated $794.2 million error. The filing establishes that cash supports payroll and operations and that $37.5 million in Belarus was subject to distribution restrictions, but it does not quantify total required or unavailable cash. Because the entire cash addition is large relative to the $115.06 base value per share, a substantial haircut could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 30, 2026 excess-cash schedule by jurisdiction covering payroll and working-capital needs, restricted or trapped balances, and repatriation taxes; rerun the bridge using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Acquired-intangible amortization may represent an economic cost stripped from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $71.367 million of FY2025 purchased-intangible amortization, equal to 18.0% of the $396.8 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If purchased-intangible amortization was added back to OE while acquisition or customer-replacement spending was excluded, sustainable OE and potentially growth are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in depreciation and amortization expense was primarily the result of increased amortization of acquired finite-lived intangible assets largely resulting from the acquisitions of NEORIS and First Derivative in the fourth quarter of 2024, partially offset by $6.3 million in lower depreciation and amortization on property and equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large recurring amortization charge, principally for acquired customer relationships, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the valuation added it back or omitted an equivalent replacement cost. At 18.0% of anchor OE, the treatment is reasonably capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2025 OE calculation to the $71.367 million purchased-intangible amortization and identify maintenance acquisition spending or a customer-attrition replacement charge; rerun OE if no equivalent economic cost is included.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring cannot be normalized as a one-off
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.893 million of FY2025 restructuring charges and $27.336 million in the first half of 2026, equal to 12.1% and 6.9% of anchor OE, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back recurring severance or optimization charges raises anchor OE and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to complete all restructuring actions commenced under the 2025 Cost Optimization Program by the end of the second quarter of 2026 and to incur additional charges of approximately $ 25.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate restructuring programs in successive years and show that the 2025 program continued through June 2026. They do not establish whether the valuation reversed these charges. If FY2025 charges were normalized away, the amount is large enough relative to anchor OE to affect the valuation conclusion; the 2026 charges are now incurred rather than merely forecast.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $47.893 million FY2025 charges through the anchor-OE reconciliation and the $27.336 million 2026 charges through any run-rate normalization; rerun with recurring optimization costs retained wherever they were added back.

audit_findings.title: The pension deficit is a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.408 million December 31, 2025 unfunded status, equal to $0.84 per diluted share and 0.73% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded pension or postemployment obligation is a senior claim that should reduce the equity bridge unless its funding is already captured in projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, the Company recorded expense of $ 12.6 million, $ 9.0 million and $ 9.4 million, respectively, related to these plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The year-end filing demonstrates a $46.408 million deficit, while the supplied bridge shows no pension deduction. At the filed scale, deducting it would reduce base value from $115.06 to approximately $114.22 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. The exact June 2026 funded status is not separately disclosed in the supplied quarterly record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 funded-status roll-forward and confirm projected contributions are not already deducted in OE; deduct the updated net deficit from the bridge to eliminate the omission.

audit_findings.title: Deferred software-license consideration is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.5 million undiscounted amount remaining at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.33 per diluted share and 0.29% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The unpaid software-license consideration is a fixed cash claim that can escape OE when the asset purchase was noncash and the later payment is classified outside operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the undiscounted deferred consideration amounts owed totaled approximately $ 30.1 million and are expected to be paid in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that $18.5 million remained payable in 2026, and the bridge does not separately deduct it. Payments already made by June reduced the reported cash balance, so only the remaining claim should be considered. Deducting $0.33 per share would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the liability was still unpaid on the valuation date and was not captured in OE or debt; deduct the remaining carrying or settlement amount from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-outs may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.312 million June 30, 2026 contingent-consideration liability, equal to $0.24 per diluted share and 0.21% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid acquisition consideration is payable before common equity and may bypass OE because settlement is classified as financing cash flow; it therefore belongs in the equity bridge unless otherwise captured.
audit_findings.evidence: In some business combinations, the Company agrees to contingent consideration arrangements and the Company determines the fair value of contingent consideration using Monte Carlo simulations (which involve a simulation of future revenues and earnings during the earn-out period using management’s best estimates) or probability-weighted expected return methods.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $13.312 million fair-value liability. The bridge contains no corresponding deduction. Although ultimate payouts are estimate-dependent, deducting the entire recorded balance would reduce value by only about $0.24 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contractual payout range and post-June settlements, reconcile them to the $13.312 million liability and OE treatment, and deduct the unpaid amount not otherwise captured in projected OE.
